The same thing ends up costing different amounts in different places because various operational expenses for datacenters are geographically variable. Specifically, the costs for electricity, cooling, labor, property purchase, and taxes differ by location. Electricity and cooling alone can constitute a third of a datacenter's total costs. For example, electricity prices vary significantly: Idaho has a low cost of 3.6¢ per KWH due to hydroelectric power not being transmitted long distances, while California's cost is 10.0¢ per KWH due to long-distance transmission, limited lines, and restrictions on coal-fired electricity. Hawaii has the highest cost at 18.0¢ per KWH because fuel must be shipped to generate electricity.
